iterations.explanation: No previous feedback was provided. Six dimensions preserve orthogonality: session control, credential lifetime, data protection, filtering, location services, and fleet observability.

clusters.name: Session Lifecycle Management
clusters.description: Session termination and inactivity policies that control authenticated user-session duration, distinct from verification-code or token validity.

relations.rationale: Authentication lifetime policies determine how long credentials remain valid, while session policies govern active authenticated sessions.

values.label: Manual session termination
values.description: Immediately invalidates the active user session when the logout action is selected.

values.label: Inactivity-based logout
values.description: Ends authenticated sessions automatically after fifteen minutes without user activity.

clusters.name: Authentication Lifetime Policy
clusters.description: Validity periods for verification codes and authentication tokens, distinct from termination of already-established user sessions.

relations.rationale: Short credential lifetimes reduce the period during which authentication material can be misused.
Credential expiration limits the duration for which authenticated access can be established or renewed.

values.label: Thirty-minute verification validity
values.description: Verification codes remain usable for a maximum of thirty minutes before requiring revalidation.

values.label: Expiring authentication tokens
values.description: Authentication tokens have enforced expiration rather than indefinite validity.

clusters.name: Sensitive Data Protection
clusters.description: Protection mechanisms for sensitive registration, personal, and payment data during transmission and storage.

relations.rationale: Encryption requirements restrict how location, account, and payment data may be transmitted or persisted.
Authentication lifetime controls reduce exposure windows for protected user data accessed through authenticated sessions.

values.label: End-to-end data encryption
values.description: Uses end-to-end encryption for data in transit and at rest, including sensitive registration information.

clusters.name: Proximity Filtering Strategy
clusters.description: Placement and implementation of radius-based constraints when retrieving nearby-bike locations.

relations.rationale: The location service supplies candidate bike positions, after which this dimension determines how the proximity constraint is applied.
Privacy and data-protection requirements constrain exposure and handling of location results.

values.label: Post-query radius filtering
values.description: Restricts returned bikes to the configured radius, with filtering performed after the location query.

clusters.name: Bike Location Service Architecture
clusters.description: Capabilities for managing bike positions and serving nearby-bike discovery queries, separate from filtering enforcement.

relations.rationale: Location-service capabilities provide the candidate positions required before proximity filtering can enforce the rider-radius constraint.
Real-time fleet monitoring consumes or complements bike-position data managed by this service.

values.label: Location management and proximity queries
values.description: Provides bike-position management and proximity-query support for discovering nearby bikes.

clusters.name: Fleet Observability Architecture
clusters.description: Aggregation and presentation of real-time bike status and usage information for operational visibility.

relations.rationale: Operational dashboards depend on aggregated fleet and usage telemetry to present current system conditions.
Aggregated operational data enables dashboards and real-time monitoring but does not determine location-query behavior.

values.label: Aggregated fleet monitoring dashboard
values.description: Aggregates usage and bike-status data into an operational dashboard supporting real-time fleet monitoring.

saturation_history.rationale: All relevant open codes are already subsumed by the existing taxonomy. Session/logout and inactivity timeout codes map to Session Lifecycle Management; verification-code and token-expiration codes map to Authentication Lifetime Policy; encryption and sensitive-information protection map to Sensitive Data Protection; radius-based, post-query, and nearby-bike query codes map to Proximity Filtering Strategy and Bike Location Service Architecture; and real-time monitoring, usage aggregation, and operational dashboard codes map to Fleet Observability Architecture. No open code introduces a distinct architectural concern beyond the current dimensions for the CityBike use case.

All relevant open codes are already subsumed by the existing taxonomy. The verification-code items, email/password login, secure transmission/storage/handling, and registration form fields fit within Session Lifecycle Management, Authentication Credential Policy, and Sensitive Data Protection. The observer-based bike-status notifications and dashboard subscription are covered by Fleet Observability Architecture. The repository-based persistence/querying of bike data and usage statistics is covered by Bike Location Service Architecture. The command pattern, state machine rental flow, QR unlock, rental lifecycle, and the separation from notification scheduling are covered by Application Architecture Pattern Strategy. The payment-related strategy/interchangeability is also covered there. The remaining form-field specifics such as optional postal code are privacy/data-minimization details that are already absorbable under Sensitive Data Protection and do not require a new dimension.
